purpose: Independent practice of D1.2 — collecting data with tally marks. Used as Lesson 2 consolidation artifact.
student_learning_goal: I can collect data and record it with tally marks.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can collect data and record it with tally marks.
header.character_watermark: Tally the Tally Cat in the top-right corner of the header, holding a clipboard with tally marks. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Look at each tally. Write the number it shows.
parts.visual_layout: Five tally diagrams stacked vertically, each ~3in × 0.8in. Tallies shown: (1) ||| = 3, (2) ||||CROSS = 5, (3) ||||CROSS || = 7, (4) ||||CROSS ||||CROSS = 10, (5) ||||CROSS ||||CROSS ||| = 13. Beside each tally, an equals sign and an empty number box.

image_placeholders.description: Five tally diagrams stacked vertically for a Grade 1 worksheet, B&W line art. Diagram 1: three vertical lines (|||). Diagram 2: four vertical lines with a fifth line crossing them all (||||CROSS). Diagram 3: ||||CROSS plus 2 more lines. Diagram 4: two ||||CROSS groups (10). Diagram 5: two ||||CROSS plus 3 more (13). Each ~3in wide × 0.8in tall. Beside each, a label '= ___' with an empty number box.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P1_TALLIES at Part 1: instructions ask the child to read each tally and write the number. Keywords name the visual elements (tally, marks).

parts.student_instructions: Pick a question. Survey 5 classmates. Draw a tally mark for each answer.
parts.visual_layout: A small chart with a question line at the top ('My question: ___') and 3 category rows below, each with: a label slot, a tally area (~3in wide), and a total box.

image_placeholders.description: A simple tally chart for a Grade 1 worksheet. At the top, a labelled line 'My question: ___'. Below, 3 category rows. Each row has: a label box on the left (~1.5in wide), a wide tally area in the middle (~3in × 0.8in for drawing tally marks), and a total box on the right (~0.8in square).
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P2_CHART at Part 2: instructions ask the child to survey classmates and tally. Keywords name the recording method (tally) and activity (survey).

parts.answer_key: Any valid tally where total tallies = 5 (matching the 5 classmates surveyed). Common: 'Favourite fruit?' Apple || (2), Banana | (1), Grape || (2). Total = 5.

parts.student_instructions: Add up these tallies. Write the total. Then draw your own tally for the number 12.
parts.visual_layout: Top half: 3 tally totaling problems. Bottom half: a blank tally area labelled 'My tally for 12'.

image_placeholders.description: Three tally-addition problems stacked vertically for a Grade 1 worksheet. Problem 1: ||||CROSS + |||| = ___ (Answer: 9). Problem 2: ||||CROSS ||||CROSS + ||| = ___ (Answer: 13). Problem 3: ||||CROSS ||||CROSS ||||CROSS = ___ (Answer: 15). Below the problems, a blank tally area ~3in × 1in labelled 'My tally for 12'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P3_TOTALS at Part 3: instructions ask the child to total tallies and draw a new one. Keywords name the activity (total, tally).

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw the tally for 20.
teacher_notes: Lesson 2 consolidation artifact. Use Part 3 as the formative signal for the no-cross trap — children who can total mixed tallies and draw 12 correctly with the 4+1 cross convention have mastered the rule.
